_doc: Worked example for common/amdahl.py: the HRX-like limits table (LEDGER 'Standing goal', refreshed 11-23, 'Now (e249)' column) with the switches live since (FLASH2_HEADPACK: verify attention 19.6, E350, live in pkg-e379, E390), one lever per part taking it to its floor at the 85 W cap (common/ceiling.py kits/qwen38-27b/lanes.json --context 81430 --prompt 81430 --device common/devices/gfx1151.json: 240 GB/s, 43.8 TFLOP/s, E369, E380). Parts without a ceiling.py floor are taken to the table's floor (prefill GDN ~3.8 s exact form, E186) or to 0 (fixed costs). Each part is its own overlap group: the parts are disjoint dispatch sets (events_summary lanes), so their savings add. 81,430-token prompt; decode per verify step at ~3.25 tokens per step (agent bench).
_discrepancy: E369 states the capped decode limit as ~92-95 ms/step: it re-floored only the matvecs (69-73 ms) and kept 228 GB/s for attention, drafter and GDN; at E380's 240 GB/s on every DRAM-bound lane the sum is 90.1. Prefill reproduces E369 (~197 -> ~128-132 s).

floors._src: levers 'to floor' take ceiling.py's lane floor at --device's profile: max(bandwidth or compute, latency chain); at cap85w no chain term binds (global_load_latency_ns unknown; the known launch + serial-issue parts are 0.03-0.23 ms/step)
